title: Reconstruction of inert operadic algebras from their color diagrams
statement:
Use the universes and monoidal infinity categories of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], with cocartesian fibrations and inner fibrations as in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. A small generalized nonsymmetric infinity operad is an inner fibration $p:\mathcal M\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ admitting cocartesian lifts of inert base arrows (opposites of consecutive-subinterval inclusions), satisfying $\mathcal M_{[n]}\simeq\mathcal M_{[1]}\times_{\mathcal M_{[0]}}\cdots\times_{\mathcal M_{[0]}}\mathcal M_{[1]}$; the zero-factor product is $\mathcal M_{[0]}$. It also satisfies this relative-limit axiom: if $I_n$ is the category of inert arrows $\alpha:[n]\to[i]$, $i=0,1$, and commuting inert triangles, and $C_\alpha$ are the cocartesian projections of $C\in\mathcal M_{[n]}$, then for every $X\in\mathcal M_{[m]}$ and $\phi:[m]\to[n]$ the canonical map $\operatorname{Map}^{\phi}(X,C)\to\lim_{\alpha\in I_n}\operatorname{Map}^{\alpha\phi}(X,C_\alpha)$ is an equivalence. The superscript denotes the homotopy fiber over the specified base arrow. An inert edge of $\mathcal M$ means a cocartesian edge over an inert base arrow. An algebra in a monoidal infinity category $\mathcal V$ is an inert-preserving functor $\mathcal M\to\mathcal V^\otimes$ over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$; write $\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal M}(\mathcal V)$ for the full infinity category on these functors. Let $\mathcal M$ be such an operad with $\mathcal M_{[0]}$ a Kan complex and let $\mathcal V$ be any monoidal infinity category. Put $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{triv}}=\mathcal M\times_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}_{\mathrm{inert}}$, regarded over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ by composition, and let $\tau:\mathcal M_{\mathrm{triv}}\to\mathcal M$ be the inclusion. Then $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{triv}}$ is a small generalized nonsymmetric infinity operad, $\tau$ preserves inert edges, and $\tau_{[0]}$ is the identity. Restriction to the fiber over $[1]$ induces a natural equivalence
$$E:\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal M_{\mathrm{triv}}}(\mathcal V)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal M_{[1]},\mathcal V).$$
Its inverse sends $P$ and an object $x$ over $[n]$ to the tuple $(P(x_1),\ldots,P(x_n))$ under $\mathcal V^\otimes_{[n]}\simeq\mathcal V^n$, with the unique empty tuple when $n=0$; on inert structure it uses the corresponding projections. The equivalence is on infinity categories, including coherent transformations and all higher simplices. No colimit or presentability hypothesis on $\mathcal V$ is imposed.

external.place: Definition 3.4.1, Lemma 3.4.4 and Proposition 3.4.5, printed pp.615–616

proof.text: Put $C=\mathcal M_{\mathrm{triv}}$, $s:C\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, and $B=\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}_{\mathrm{inert}}$. All fibers and all simplices over inert base diagrams are inherited from $\mathcal M$. The map $C\to B$ is an inner fibration by pullback. The composite $s$ is also inner: in a lifting problem over a simplex of $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, an inner horn in $C$ contains all consecutive spine edges, so those base edges are inert. Their composites are inert too, and the whole prescribed base simplex lies in $B$; hence the original inner-fibration filler lies in $C$. Smallness is inherited. For fixed endpoints, the right-pinched mapping-space model has the same simplices as $\mathcal M$ over an inert arrow and none over a noninert arrow: its base simplices are degeneracies of that single arrow in the nerve of the ordinary base category.

source.place: Supporting operadic foundation for paragraph 2; Gepner–Haugseng Definition 3.4.1, Remark 3.4.3, Lemma 3.4.4 and Proposition 3.4.5, printed pp.615–616. General relative-Kan inputs: Kerodon 02XT, 0302; HTT 4.3.2.15, 4.3.2.18. These are not Stacks results.

proof.text: Each original cocartesian lift $u:x\to y$ over an inert $\rho:[n]\to[m]$ stays $s$-cocartesian. Indeed, for $z$ over $[k]$, apply [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] over each discrete base arrow $\psi:[m]\to[k]$. If $\psi$ is inert, the two mapping fibers in its criterion are unchanged and the required equivalence is the original one. Otherwise both are empty: $\psi\rho$ is inert if and only if $\psi$ is inert, indeed, if $\rho^{\mathrm{op}}(j)=a+j$, then $(\psi\rho)^{\mathrm{op}}(j)=a+\psi^{\mathrm{op}}(j)$, so the successive increments are identical, also when $k=0$. This proves the mapping square for $s$. Conversely any $s$-cocartesian lift over $\rho$ has target equivalent, in the unchanged fiber, to the target of an original lift: both are initial in the lift category $L(x,\rho)$ formed in $C$ by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality]. Its image in $\mathcal M$ is therefore cocartesian by the mapping criterion. Thus $\tau$ preserves inert edges, and $\tau_{[0]}$ is literally the identity. The Segal fiber-product axiom uses these same lifts and unchanged fibers, so is inherited. For the incidence axiom over an inert $\phi:[m]\to[n]$, all composites $\alpha\phi$ are inert and every mapping fiber and its coherence maps are unchanged; use the incidence axiom for $\mathcal M$. For noninert $\phi$ the left side is empty. Necessarily $n>0$, since every map to $[0]$ is inert. At least one $\rho_i\phi$ is noninert: if all restrictions of $\phi^{\mathrm{op}}$ to adjacent pairs had increment one, then $\phi^{\mathrm{op}}(j)=\phi^{\mathrm{op}}(0)+j$ would be a consecutive inclusion. The incidence diagram therefore has an empty color term, making its limit empty as well. This proves the relative-limit axiom, including $n=0$ where $I_0$ is the identity projection and no noninert case exists. Consequently $C$ is a small generalized nonsymmetric infinity operad with the same Kan zero-fiber.

source.place: Supporting operadic foundation for paragraph 2; Gepner–Haugseng Definition 3.4.1, Remark 3.4.3, Lemma 3.4.4 and Proposition 3.4.5, printed pp.615–616. General relative-Kan inputs: Kerodon 02XT, 0302; HTT 4.3.2.15, 4.3.2.18. These are not Stacks results.

proof.text: Write $C=\mathcal M_{\mathrm{triv}}$, $A=\mathcal M_{[1]}$, and $s:C\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$. The inclusion $A\subset C$ is full, since the only inert endomorphism of $[1]$ is the identity. For $x\in C_{[n]}$, choose inert lifts $\alpha_i:x\to c_i$ over $\rho_i$. Its local coslice $J_x=A\times_C C_{x/}$ decomposes as the disjoint union of the categories of arrows over $\rho_i$, $1\leq i\leq n$: every inert map $[n]\to[1]$ is one of these, and every simplex of $A$ projects to the identity of $[1]$, so the index cannot change along a simplex. Regard $C\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}_{\mathrm{inert}}$ as an inner fibration. Each component is precisely the lift category $L(x,\rho_i)$ of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality]; that node makes $\alpha_i$ initial in it, including all higher triangles. Therefore [lem-coef-relative-limit-initial-components] applies to the inclusion $\{\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n\}\to J_x$. Now fix any $h:A\to\mathcal V$. For $p:\mathcal V^\otimes\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, the local boundary is $h$ after target projection, and the prescribed base cone is $sl_x$. Over the selected initial objects its values are $h(c_i)$ and its base edges are $\rho_i$. The Segal equivalence in [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category] gives a tuple $v_x\in\mathcal V^\otimes_{[n]}$ with these components; choosing the fiber equivalences and the cocartesian projections gives a cone with exactly these targets and base edges. Its relative-limit clause makes this a $p$-limit cone. Here and below, the relative-limit clause of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category] is stated by mapping spaces from single objects $D$ over each base arrow $\phi$. By [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-constant-test] (its limit dual) this is the same as being a $p$-limit diagram in the sense of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone] for the cone on the discrete set of projections: for discrete $K=I_{\mathrm{disc}}$, $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal V^\otimes)}(\Delta_KD,f)$ is the product of the $\operatorname{Map}(D,f_i)$. The lower row of the test square lies in the discrete mapping sets of $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, so the square is a homotopy pullback exactly when its fiber maps over every $\phi$ are equivalences. That fiberwise condition is the displayed product condition. The case $n=0$ is the empty cone. (If the chosen targets are merely equivalent, compose the projections with those fiber equivalences; the dual of clause (1) of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence] preserves the relative-limit condition.) The initial-components theorem supplies a local $p$-limit lift on the entire $J_x$. For $n=0$, $J_x$ is empty and the monoidal empty-product clause supplies its required relative limit over $[0]$. The map $p$ is an isofibration: it is inner by its monoidal fibration hypothesis, and every equivalence in $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ is an identity, lifted to an equivalence by a degenerate edge. The right-hand clause of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-kan-existence], with this full inclusion and these local lifts, gives an exact extension $H:C\to\mathcal V^\otimes$ of $h$, over $s$, right Kan extended relative to $p$. Thus every color diagram satisfies the existence hypothesis of [lem-coef-relative-right-kan-restriction].

source.place: Supporting operadic foundation for paragraph 2; Gepner–Haugseng Definition 3.4.1, Remark 3.4.3, Lemma 3.4.4 and Proposition 3.4.5, printed pp.615–616. General relative-Kan inputs: Kerodon 02XT, 0302; HTT 4.3.2.15, 4.3.2.18. These are not Stacks results.

proof.text: We identify the full subcategory of relative right Kan extensions in step 3 with $\operatorname{Alg}_C(\mathcal V)$. If $H$ preserves inert edges, its cone on the $\alpha_i$ consists of $p$-cocartesian projections; [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category] says that this is a relative $p$-limit cone, in the diagram sense by [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-constant-test]: for the discrete color diagram the upper-right test mapping space is the product of its component mapping spaces, and the fiber of the test square over each base arrow $\phi$ is exactly the product equivalence in the monoidal axiom. This also verifies the relative-limit property of the comparison tuple cone used below. The particular-cone clause of [lem-coef-relative-limit-initial-components] makes the full cone $Hl_x$ a $p$-limit. Conversely, suppose $H$ is relatively right Kan extended. The same clause says that the cone $H(x)\to H(c_i)$ is a $p$-limit. Compare it to the monoidal tuple with components $H(c_i)$ and its cocartesian projections. The relative universal property in [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone] supplies comparison maps over the identity of $[n]$ fixing the targets and their cone data in both directions. Their composites equal the identities up to coherent homotopy, since that same mapping-space universal property makes the space of comparisons over fixed identity data contractible. Hence the comparison of apices is an equivalence in the fiber, and every $H(\alpha_i)$ is $p$-cocartesian by the mapping criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]. This holds for every chosen inert lift to a color; a different lift over the same $\rho_i$ differs by an equivalence of targets, by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality], so its image is cocartesian as well. To check an arbitrary inert edge $a:x\to y$ over $\rho:[n]\to[m]$, compose with the color projections $b_j:y\to d_j$. Each $b_ja$ is a cocartesian lift of the corresponding selected color projection from $x$, by the composition clause of that node, so $H(b_ja)$ and $H(b_j)$ are cocartesian. Choose a $p$-cocartesian lift $H(x)\to z$ over $\rho$. The object case of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] factors $H(a)$ through a map $t:z\to H(y)$ in the fiber over $[m]$, with its coherent triangle. Write $v:H(x)\to z$ for the chosen lift and choose cocartesian projections $\delta_j:z\to z_j$. Their composites $\delta_jv$ are cocartesian over $\rho_j\rho$. The object transport formula factors $H(b_j)t:z\to H(d_j)$ through $\delta_j$ as a fiber map $\theta_j:z_j\to H(d_j)$, with its coherent triangle. Composing with $v$ identifies $\theta_j\delta_jv$ with $H(b_ja)$. Both $\delta_jv$ and $H(b_ja)$ are cocartesian lifts from $H(x)$ over the same map $\rho_j\rho$, so both are initial in $L(H(x),\rho_j\rho)$ by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality]. Its comparison clause makes $\theta_j$ an equivalence of targets. Under the Segal identifications determined by $\delta_j$ and $H(b_j)$, these $\theta_j$ are precisely the components of $t$. The Segal equivalence $\mathcal V^\otimes_{[m]}\simeq\mathcal V^m$ then makes $t$ an equivalence. Thus $H(a)$ is cocartesian, by the mapping criterion, as required. For $m=0$ this is the empty tuple and every map in its point fiber is an equivalence. The two full subcategories therefore coincide, on all transformations as well as objects. Apply [lem-coef-relative-right-kan-restriction]: restriction from this algebra category to color functors is a trivial Kan fibration, hence fully faithful and essentially surjective with its complete coherent simplicial data. The degree-one target fiber is $\mathcal V$, so this is the asserted equivalence. It is natural in $\mathcal M$: restriction to colors commutes with precomposition by every operad map, and these are the actual restriction functors on both sides. An empty color category gives only degree zero and the same empty-cone argument applies.

source.place: Supporting operadic foundation for paragraph 2; Gepner–Haugseng Definition 3.4.1, Remark 3.4.3, Lemma 3.4.4 and Proposition 3.4.5, printed pp.615–616. General relative-Kan inputs: Kerodon 02XT, 0302; HTT 4.3.2.15, 4.3.2.18. These are not Stacks results.

proof.text: Let $E$ be restriction to $A=\mathcal M_{[1]}$. The previous step proves this actual restriction functor is an equivalence on infinity categories. For an extension of $P:A\to\mathcal V$, its inert projections at $x\in C_{[n]}$ are cocartesian, so the monoidal Segal equivalence in [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category] identifies its value with $(P(x_1),\ldots,P(x_n))$. For any inert $a:x\to y$ over $[n]\to[m]$, compose with each color projection of $y$; each resulting composite is an inert lift of the corresponding color projection of $x$. By [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality], its comparison with the chosen lift is an equivalence in the lift category, retaining the commuting triangle. Applying the extension functor retains that triangle and equivalence. Thus its image agrees, under the Segal identifications and these comparisons, with the projection to the indicated consecutive subtuple; this is an agreement up to coherent equivalence, not an equality of arbitrary chosen representatives. At $n=0$ the target fiber is equivalent to the point and this is the unique empty tuple, with contractible choices of representatives. Coherent quasi-inverses and their transformations exist by the restriction equivalence, rather than by choosing objectwise formulas without coherence. Naturality follows because restriction commutes with precomposition by operad maps and with inert-preserving monoidal postcomposition, including parameter simplices. No colimits or presentability entered: the only limits used were the relative tuple cones that are part of the monoidal axioms.

split_report.summary: Proved the inert-truncation axioms directly, then constructed and classified inert algebra extensions by existing local relative-limit, relative-Kan existence, and coherent restriction results. Spelled out the inverse, transformations and empty arity. No statement change or new nodes. The nearby inert-operadic-algebra-classification cannot be cited here because its statement dependency on operadic-algebra-presentability would create a cycle; its definitions are already inline in this item.
